title: Wings Food Safety Quiz
description: Handling raw wings: hand washing, the Food Safety Mitt, the fryer process, the blue towel and keeping raw away from ready-to-eat. Answer each question, then check it. You will see straight away whether you got it right and why.

questions.title: What is the very first step before handling any raw wing product?
choices: Grab the fry basket
Put on gloves
Wash and sanitize hands at the dedicated hand sink
Pull wings from freezer
questions.explanation: Hands first, at the hand sink, every time. Gloves go on after — a glove pulled over an unwashed hand just moves the germs somewhere you cannot see them.

questions.title: What is the purpose of the Food Safety Mitt when grabbing wings?
choices: To protect your hand from the cold freezer
To keep your hands dry
To keep the wings from thawing
To maintain plastic-to-plastic contact with the bag and prevent bare-hand contact with raw chicken
questions.explanation: It is not for the cold. It keeps plastic on plastic so your skin never touches raw chicken, which is how raw chicken ends up on everything you touch next.

questions.title: When getting wings out of the freezer, you should use the hand that has the Mitt on it to open the freezer door.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: The other hand opens the door. The mitt hand is the one going near the raw product — put it on the door handle and you have just made the handle a raw chicken surface for everybody after you.

questions.title: After using the Food Safety Mitt to remove wings from the freezer, what do you do with it?
choices: Hang it back up for the next cook
Shake it off and discard it along with the plastic bag
Rinse it and reuse it
Set it on the prep station
questions.explanation: Shake it off and bin it with the bag. It touched raw chicken, so it is finished — hanging it back up or rinsing it carries that straight to the next person.

questions.title: Which hand do you use to grab wings when wearing the Food Safety Mitt?
choices: Your non-dominant hand only
Either hand — it does not matter
Both hands
The hand with the mitt on it
questions.explanation: Only the mitt hand goes near the wings. The whole point is one hand stays clean for doors, handles and everything else.

questions.title: Where must you fill the fry basket with wings before dropping them?
choices: Over the sink
On top of the freezer lid
Over the sheet pan at the fry prep station
Over the fryer so crumbs fall into the oil
questions.explanation: Over the sheet pan at the fry prep station, so whatever falls lands somewhere you can clean. Over the fryer it goes in the oil, over the sink or the freezer lid it goes everywhere.

questions.title: If a cook is NOT using the Food Safety Mitt process, when must they wash and sanitize hands and wipe down the area?
choices: Every 30 minutes on a set schedule
Only at the end of the batch
Only if they touched their face
Before product finishes cooking AND before moving to any non-prep area
questions.explanation: Before the product is out of the fryer, and again before going anywhere else in the kitchen. Waiting for the end of the batch means raw chicken has been on your hands the whole time.

questions.title: What colour sanitizer towel is used to clean the raw prep area, and where can it be used?
choices: Green towel — used on the fryer and prep station
Any colour towel — colour does not matter
Blue towel — used on raw prep areas only
Blue towel — used anywhere in the kitchen
questions.explanation: Blue, and only on raw prep areas. The colour is the whole system — it is how anyone can see at a glance that a towel has been on raw chicken.

questions.title: Which surfaces must be wiped with the blue sanitizer towel during the sanitization step?
choices: Fryer, fryer control panel, fry basket handle, bump bar pad, prep station, and freezer door handle
Fryer and freezer door handle only
Just the prep station surface
Prep station and sink area
questions.explanation: All six. The ones people forget are the control panel and the bump bar pad, because they are touched with the same hands and never look dirty.

questions.title: How often must the raw prep area be wiped down during continuous use?
choices: Every two hours, or more often as build-up occurs
Every 30 minutes
Once per shift
Only when visibly soiled
questions.explanation: Every two hours at the least, and sooner if it is building up. "When it looks dirty" is too late — by then it has been dirty for a while.

questions.title: What is the most critical rule about the blue sanitizer towel to prevent cross-contamination?
choices: Rinse it between uses
Replace it every hour
Use it only on raw prep areas — never on ready-to-eat food areas or shared surfaces
Store it on top of the fryer between uses
questions.explanation: It never leaves the raw area. One wipe of the make table with a blue towel takes raw chicken straight to food that is going out the door as it is.
